title: Pumpkin seeds: protein, zinc, magnesium, and calories

seo.title: Pumpkin seeds: protein, zinc, magnesium, and calories
seo.meta_description: Hulled pumpkin seeds provide about 30 g protein, 550–600 mg magnesium, and 7–8 mg zinc per 100 g. A 1-ounce serving gives a more useful picture.
seo.search_intent: Understand the protein, magnesium, zinc, fat, and calories in hulled pumpkin seeds and translate 100 g figures into a realistic serving.

excerpt: Pumpkin seed kernels are nutrient-dense: roughly 30 g protein, 49 g fat, and more than 550 mg magnesium per 100 g. A 1-ounce serving is about 8–9 g protein and 160–170 calories.
content_html:
Pumpkin seed kernels pack a lot into a small amount: roughly 30 g protein, 49 g fat, and 559–574 calories per 100 g. That concentration explains both their nutrient density and their energy density.

What hulled pumpkin seeds provide

NutrientPer 100 gPer 1 oz (28 g)
Calories~559–574 kcal~157–161 kcal
Protein~30 g~8.4 g
Fat~49 g~13.7 g
Fiber~6–6.5 g~1.7–1.8 g
Magnesium~550–592 mg~154–166 mg
Zinc~7.6–7.8 mg~2.1–2.2 mg

Raw and roasted entries differ slightly, but not enough to change the overall picture: pumpkin seed kernels are especially rich in magnesium and also contribute zinc and protein.

A one-ounce serving puts 100 g data in context

Thirty grams of protein per 100 g sounds comparable with some high-protein foods until you remember that 100 g pumpkin seeds contains well over 550 calories. One ounce gives about 8–9 g protein for around 160 calories.

To obtain 30 g protein from pumpkin seeds alone would require about 100 g and more than 550 calories. They work very well as a protein-rich addition, but they are rarely the most efficient sole protein source for a meal.

Magnesium is where pumpkin seeds really stand out

With roughly 550–592 mg magnesium per 100 g, one ounce can supply around 154–166 mg. That is a large amount from a compact serving.

They also provide phosphorus, iron, copper, manganese, potassium, and zinc. As with other plant foods, the amount listed in a composition table is not identical to the amount absorbed; phytate and the overall meal affect mineral bioavailability.

Zinc adds another useful mineral

Hulled seeds provide roughly 7.6–7.8 mg zinc per 100 g. One ounce contains about 2.1–2.2 mg. Plant-based zinc absorption can be lower in high-phytate diets, so the number on the label is only one part of the story.

Most of the calories come from fat

About 49 g fat per 100 g accounts for roughly 441 calories before protein and carbohydrate are counted. Most of the fat is unsaturated.

“High calorie” and “nutritionally empty” are not synonyms. Pumpkin seeds combine their calories with protein, minerals, and predominantly unsaturated fat.

Whole seeds and kernels are not interchangeable database entries

A USDA-derived whole-seed reference contains about 18.4 g fiber and 19.4 g fat/100 g, versus roughly 6–6.5 g fiber and 49 g fat/100 g in hulled kernels. Check which form a nutrition table describes.

The useful takeaway

Pumpkin seeds stand out for magnesium, zinc, protein, and unsaturated fat. Per 100 g data are useful for comparisons, but a 1-ounce serving gives a better sense of how much protein, minerals, and energy you are actually eating.

faq.question: How much protein is in pumpkin seeds?
faq.answer: Hulled pumpkin seeds provide about 30 g per 100 g, or about 8–9 g in a 1-ounce serving.

faq.question: Are pumpkin seeds high in magnesium?
faq.answer: Yes. They commonly provide about 550–592 mg per 100 g, or roughly 154–166 mg per ounce.

faq.question: How many calories are in an ounce?
faq.answer: About 157–161 calories for hulled pumpkin seeds, depending on whether they are raw or roasted.
